title: U.S. House · Virginia's 2nd District
area: Virginia's 2nd Congressional District (Virginia Beach and the Eastern Shore)

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Jennifer Kiggans advanced unopposed. Elaine Luria won the Democratic primary on August 4, 2026 with 80.4% of the vote. This is a rematch of the 2022 race, which Kiggans won 52% to 48% over then-incumbent Luria. Ballotpedia identified this as a battleground race; Trump carried the district by 0.2 points in 2024.

summary.text: Jennifer Kiggans is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Virginia's 2nd District, a Navy veteran and nurse practitioner who served in the Virginia Senate before winning the House seat in 2022. According to her official biography, she sits on the Armed Services, Veterans' Affairs, and Natural Resources Committees. Her campaign website describes her priorities as lowering the cost of living, growing jobs, and government oversight.

background.text: Born in Tampa, Florida in 1971 and graduated from high school in Orlando, Florida.

Earned a bachelor's degree in international relations from Boston University (1993), a bachelor's degree in nursing from Old Dominion University (2011), and a master's degree in nursing from Vanderbilt University (2012). After college she taught English in Japan through the JET Programme in 1993-1994.
Served 10 years in the U.S. Navy as a helicopter pilot, flying H-46 and H-3 aircraft and completing two deployments to the Persian Gulf, before leaving active duty in 2003.

Used her GI Bill benefits to train as a board-certified adult-geriatric primary care nurse practitioner, providing care to seniors in long-term care facilities and private practice in Virginia Beach and Norfolk.

Won the 2019 Republican primary for Virginia's 7th Senate District over Virginia Beach School Board member Carolyn Weems, 52% to 48%, and the November 2019 general election over Democrat Cheryl Turpin; she served in the Virginia Senate beginning in 2020.
Won the 2022 Republican primary for Virginia's 2nd District and defeated Democratic incumbent Elaine Luria in the general election; she took office in January 2023 and was re-elected in 2024.
Serves on the House Armed Services, Veterans' Affairs, and Natural Resources Committees, according to her official biography.
According to her official biography, she and her husband, a former F/A-18 pilot, live in Virginia Beach and have four grown children.

priorities.text: Says her priority is "lowering costs, putting more money back in your pocket, standing up for our families, and working across the aisle to deliver real results."
priorities.quote: My priority will always be lowering costs, putting more money back in your pocket, standing up for our families, and working across the aisle to deliver real results.

priorities.text: Says she "fought to pass legislation to protect working families and small businesses from government overreach, reduce executive branch overspending, and bring much-needed oversight to federal agencies."
priorities.quote: fought to pass legislation to protect working families and small businesses from government overreach, reduce executive branch overspending, and bring much-needed oversight to federal agencies

positions.summary: Says she led a bipartisan effort to renew and reform the Affordable Care Act tax credits and co-led a framework to extend premium tax credit relief, and also says she opposes Medicare for All.
positions.quote: Jen led the bipartisan effort to renew and reform the Affordable Care Act (ACA) tax credits.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Armed Services (Subcommittees on Seapower and Projection Forces, Military Personnel, and Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation), the House Committee on Natural Resources (Subcommittees on Water, Wildlife, and Fisheries, and Energy & Mineral Resources), and the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs, where she chairs the Subcommittee on Oversight & Investigations, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Elaine Luria
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 80.4% of the vote

summary.text: Elaine Luria is a retired Navy commander and former Democratic U.S. Representative for Virginia's 2nd District (2019-2023). She won the seat in 2018, was re-elected in 2020, and lost it to Jennifer Kiggans in 2022; this year she won the Democratic primary and is seeking a rematch. Her campaign website says she is running on lowering costs, making health care more affordable, and supporting veterans and military families.

background.text: Born in Birmingham, Alabama in 1975 and graduated from Indian Springs School in 1993.

Graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy in 1997 with a bachelor's degree in physics and history, and earned a master's degree in engineering management from Old Dominion University in 2004 while serving in the Navy.

Served 20 years in the U.S. Navy, mostly aboard combat ships as a nuclear-trained surface warfare officer, rising to the rank of commander; her campaign website says she deployed six times, and Wikipedia reports she commanded Assault Craft Unit Two from 2014 until retiring in 2017.
After retiring in 2017, founded an arts and crafts business called Mermaid Factory in Hampton Roads.
Ran for Congress in 2018, defeating Republican incumbent Scott Taylor, and won re-election against him in 2020.

Represented Virginia's 2nd District from 2019 to 2023, serving on the House Committees on Veterans' Affairs, Homeland Security, and Armed Services and chairing the Veterans' Affairs Subcommittee on Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs.

Was an original member of the Select Committee to Investigate the January 6 Attack on the United States Capitol, appointed in 2021, and was elected vice chair of the Armed Services Committee for the 117th Congress, according to Wikipedia.
Lost re-election to Jennifer Kiggans in 2022, 52% to 48%, and won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 80.4% of the vote.

priorities.text: Is campaigning on healthcare costs and access, saying "people's healthcare is getting cut, and people's healthcare is getting more expensive."
priorities.quote: People's healthcare is getting cut, and people's healthcare is getting more expensive. And that's just the tip of the iceberg. There's so much that needs to be done for the American people, for the Hampton Roads community.

priorities.text: Is campaigning on government transparency, including a proposal to ban members of Congress, congressional staff, and executive branch officials from trading on political prediction markets using nonpublic information.
priorities.quote: Members of Congress, congressional staff, executive branch employees, and political appointees should not use nonpublic information to buy, sell, or exchange prediction market contracts related to political outcomes or government policy.

positions.summary: Says she would protect Medicaid, restore the Affordable Care Act subsidies, and expand the number of drugs Medicare can negotiate.
positions.quote: It means protecting Medicaid and restoring Obamacare subsidies so that working and middle class Virginians can afford high-quality, low-cost health insurance.

positions.summary: Says she believes in a woman’s right to choose and would vote again for legislation to codify abortion protections nationwide.
positions.quote: I believe strongly in a woman’s right to choose and make decisions for herself about her own body.

positions.summary: Calls for repealing the Trump administration tariffs, saying they raise costs for families.
positions.quote: And it means repealing Trump’s tariffs that are making everyday goods and everyday life so much more expensive for families.

positions.summary: Calls for repealing the 2025 tax cuts for billionaires so that health care funding can be restored.
positions.quote: That means repealing billionaire tax cuts so we can restore funding for health care

positions.summary: Says federal, state and local governments should make it as easy as possible to build new homes by cutting red tape.
positions.quote: We also need to ensure that at the federal, state, and local level we are making it as easy as possible to build new homes by cutting red tape and making sure bureaucracy isn’t getting in the way of growth.

candidates.name: J. Matt Baker

summary.text: J. Matt Baker is an independent candidate for Virginia's 2nd District who describes himself as a Naval Academy graduate, retired Marine Corps colonel, and grid-modernization engineer. He says he is running on fiscal accountability, defense oversight, and a campaign that takes no PAC money.

background.text: Graduated from Balboa High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the U.S. Naval Academy in 1987, a graduate degree from the University of Maryland in 1988, and a graduate degree from Old Dominion University in 2001.

Served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1987 to 2015. In his Ballotpedia survey, he says he served 28 years as an infantry officer, commanded 1,200 Marines and Sailors in combat in Afghanistan's Helmand Province, and retired as a colonel in 2015 after commanding the Security Cooperation Group at Fort Story.

Lists his profession as engineer; says he has spent the past 11 years modernizing electric power infrastructure for utilities, the military, energy storage companies, and universities, and that he and his wife have lived in Hampton Roads for 14 years and raised three children there.

priorities.text: Says he is running as an independent who takes no PAC money and answers to the people he represents rather than a party.
priorities.quote: This campaign takes no PAC money — not corporate, not party, not billionaire super PACs.

priorities.text: Says his priorities in Washington are real oversight of defense spending, utility rate reform on data centers, and federal cost-sharing on flood infrastructure.
priorities.quote: real oversight of defense spending, utility rate reform on data centers, and federal cost-sharing on flood infrastructure this region has funded alone.

positions.summary: Says abortion decisions belong to the woman and her physician rather than to Washington or state legislatures, and that he would not support a federal ban.
positions.quote: This decision belongs to the woman, in consultation with her physician and her faith — not to Washington, and not to fifty statehouses deciding which medications she can buy or which state lines she can cross for care.

positions.summary: Opposes tariffs imposed by presidential decree, while saying he is not against narrow tariffs that Congress legislates.
positions.quote: I'm not against narrow tariffs Congress actually legislates. I'm against a President taxing every family by decree, changing the rate more than fifty times, and calling it a strategy.

positions.summary: Says he would support Congress reasserting its role with votes on the use of force.
positions.quote: I'd support reasserting Congress's role: real votes on the use of force, not after-the-fact briefings;

positions.summary: Supports federal incentives for localities that cut permitting timelines and update zoning, but not federal zoning mandates.
positions.quote: I'd push for federal incentives that reward localities for cutting permitting timelines and updating outdated zoning that blocks starter homes and multifamily construction — incentives, not federal zoning mandates from Washington.

statements.quote: Climate Change is Real. Norfolk has the highest rate of sea-level rise on the East Coast. Hampton Roads floods on sunny days.
I'd fix that math, push more of that fund straight to keeping doors open and staff paid, and fight further Medicaid cuts rural and coastal facilities can't absorb.
statements.context: In the VPM/WHRO questionnaire, on hospitals at risk from Medicaid changes

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from the VPM/WHRO candidate questionnaire (updated Sept. 30, 2026) and Baker's campaign website. No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey was found. No direct statements were found on immigration, rent regulation, minimum wage or voter citizenship proof.

candidates.name: Bishop Staten

summary.text: Bishop Staten, a Suffolk, Virginia civil servant and community activist, is an independent candidate for Virginia's 2nd Congressional District, campaigning on affordability, public safety, and equal opportunity.

background.text: Born and raised in the Hampton Roads area of Virginia (Suffolk); graduated from Nansemond River High School; has worked as a civil servant.
Describes himself as the youngest person to run for mayor of Suffolk, in 2016 at age 30, and as the runner-up in a race for Commissioner of the Revenue with 10,909 votes.

In his Ballotpedia survey, lists a short stint with the NFL's Baltimore Ravens, work as a public-address announcer for Kings Fork girls' and boys' basketball, and service as secretary of a nonprofit organization, the PPPCP; says his first job was as a car hop at Sonic Drive-In.

priorities.text: Lists his campaign's key messages as "Purpose Over Politics" and giving Hampton Roads a congressional candidate from within the district.
Says he is personally passionate about affordability, public safety, and equal opportunity.
priorities.quote: Affordability, Public Safety and Equal Opportunity

positions.summary: Says he will allow women to make decisions about their bodies.
positions.quote: I will allow women to make the decisions when it comes to their bodies. Women's rights are important to me.

positions.summary: Answered a question about hospital and health care funding with a call for Medicare for All.
Answered a question about housing with a call for a national rent freeze and an eviction moratorium.
positions.quote: National rent freeze and moratorium on evictions.

statements.quote: Restore Congress's authority over broad tariffs.
statements.context: In the VPM/WHRO questionnaire, on trade policy

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from the VPM/WHRO candidate questionnaire (Sept. 24, 2026); his answers are brief. He has no campaign website that could be loaded. No stance was found on guns, immigration, taxes or school choice.
